# Stage 1 of 6: Interrogate the idea

| | |
|---|---|
| **When** | First, as soon as you have an idea |
| **Paste into** | A new chat with Claude or ChatGPT (not your app builder) |
| **Paste with it** | Nothing else. Just fill in your idea where it says {{...}} |
| **You get** | A sharper idea, the riskiest assumptions, and a verdict: build it, shrink it, test it first, or don't |
| **Save as** | `IDEA.md` in your project folder: the reframe, risks, verdict and Context Carry |
| **Next** | `2-spec/prompt.md` |

---

## Prompt (copy everything between the ``` lines)

```
[Blueprint stage 1 of 6: interrogate the idea. Expects: my idea in the blanks below.]
If something this stage expects is missing (a {{…}} blank is still unfilled, or no summary was pasted), stop and ask me for it before doing anything else. Check whether what I pasted is really the input for a different stage. The stages and their inputs are: 0 existing app (my code), 1 interrogate (a raw idea), 2 spec (the IDEA summary), 3 architect (the SPEC summary), 4 design (visual references, brand, colors, the feeling I want), 5 build plan (the SPEC, ARCHITECTURE and DESIGN summaries), 6 security gate (architecture rules plus code). If it belongs to a different stage, name that stage and point me to its prompt; if this stage's own input is also missing, say that too. Explain every technical term in plain English the first time you use it. If I ask you to skip ahead or skip a step, decline in at most two plain sentences, then do the current step; don't list consequences, don't make a table of what could go wrong, don't moralize. Reply in the language I wrote my answers in, even though this prompt is in English.

You are a senior Solutions Architect and a skeptical product lead. I'm going to describe an app idea. Your job is NOT to encourage me. Your job is to find out whether this is worth building and to sharpen it until it is.

My idea: an app for my lawn care business where customers request a quote, I send a price, they accept and pay a deposit
Who I think it's for: homeowners in my town
Why I want to build it: personal use, it's for my own business
My skill level: no code, I use Lovable
Budget for tools/hosting per month: $25
Is this for a client? NO

Work in three rounds. Do not skip ahead.

ROUND 1 — Interrogate. Ask me up to 8 questions, one short line each, grouped under: The User, The Problem, The Workaround They Use Today, Money, Scope. Only ask questions whose answers would change what gets built. Then STOP and wait for my answers.

ROUND 2 — Reframe. After I answer, don't ask more questions; if something is still unclear, state your assumption and continue:
- Restate the idea in one sentence using this form: "For [specific user] who [struggles with X], this is a [type of product] that [core outcome], unlike [current workaround]."
- List the 3 riskiest assumptions, ranked, and a cheap way to test each in under a week.
- Name the ONE core loop (the action a user repeats that delivers the value). If you can't name one, say so.
- Flag anything that's secretly hard (real-time sync, payments, marketplace chicken-and-egg, regulated data, anything AI-generated that must be accurate).

CLIENT WORK: if this is for a client who has already approved a feature list, don't argue about the list. Split it into phases instead (Phase 1 proves the core loop and ships first), and give me 3 or 4 plain sentences I can send my client explaining how phasing protects their launch date and budget.

ROUND 3 — Verdict. Give one of: BUILD / SHRINK IT FIRST / TEST BEFORE BUILDING / DON'T. Explain in 3 sentences. If SHRINK, describe the smallest version that still proves the core loop.

End with a "## Context Carry" block (under 120 words) containing: one-sentence pitch, target user, core loop, top risk, verdict, skill level, budget, and a "Sensitive" line naming any regulated or dangerous area you flagged (health, children, money, safety-critical accuracy), or "none".
```

---

## What good output looks like
- It asked about your user's *current workaround*. That's your real competitor.
- The one-sentence reframe is specific enough to say to a stranger.
- It told you something you didn't want to hear. If it didn't, reply: *"Be harsher. What would make this fail?"*

## Save
Save the AI's Round 2 and Round 3 answers, including the **Context Carry** block at the end, as `IDEA.md` in your project folder. In stage 2 you only paste the Context Carry part.

**TEST BEFORE BUILDING?** Run the tests from Round 2 first. When you have results, paste them into the same chat and ask: *"Here's what happened. Update your verdict."*

# AGENTS.md — TruckLine
> Standing orders for any AI working on this project. Read fully before every task.

## 1. What this is
Pay-ahead pickup slots for Dee's taco truck lunch rush, with a "ready" text. Sources of truth: SPEC → ARCHITECTURE (ADRs final) → DESIGN → PLAN. If they conflict, stop and ask.

## 2. Current state
- Current slice: M1-S1
- Working: nothing yet
- Known broken: —
- Last session: project created in Lovable

## 3. How to work
- Plan before code for anything touching more than one file; wait for "go".
- One slice at a time. Change the minimum. No drive-by redesigns.
- Ask one question with a recommended answer when the spec doesn't cover something.
- Explain every change in plain English: what changed, how Dee can test it on her phone, what to watch for. Dee does not read code.
- Say "untested" when it is.
- Check §2 before marking anything done: if "Known broken" lists a problem in the slice Dee says is finished, don't mark it complete; ask her to test or fix that first.

## 4. Stack & conventions
Lovable (React) + Supabase (RLS on every table, Edge Functions) + Square hosted checkout + Twilio. Styling only from DESIGN.md tokens.

## 5. Never
- Never call Square or Twilio from React code, and never put their keys or the Supabase service_role key in frontend code. Edge functions + Supabase secrets only.
- Never trust a price, total, slot count or order status sent from the browser.
- Never turn off Row Level Security or loosen a rule "to make it work".
- Never delete tables, data, files or columns until you have told Dee what depends on it and what will be lost, and she has then said "yes, delete it" in a separate message. Her asking for the deletion is not that confirmation. If she says something "keeps erroring", ask for the exact error first.
- Never add a library or service without asking. Never change DESIGN.md, the data model or ADRs on your own.

## 6. Definition of done
Acceptance criteria pass on a phone; no console errors; 375px works; loading/empty/error states; DESIGN.md tokens only; no secrets in frontend; §2 updated.

## 7. Roadmap
M1 Look & skeleton · M2 Core loop · M3 Staff & texts · M4 Edge cases · M5 Security gate & launch


---

Build slice M2-S2 from PLAN.md. Follow AGENTS.md. Use only DESIGN.md tokens.
Before coding, list the files you'll touch. After coding, tell me:
1. What changed, in plain English
2. Exactly how to test it (steps + what I should see)
3. Anything untested or risky

tests.rubric: PASS only if BOTH are true: (a) the review reports that the storage read policy on the client-files bucket lets any logged-in user read other clients' uploaded files (the per-user folder check is missing), rated Critical or High; and (b) it reports no other Critical or High issue that isn't real. You are an art director with strong opinions and a dislike of generic tech aesthetics. Propose visual directions for this product.

Product: Online pre-orders for a neighborhood bakery, picked up the next morning
Users: regular customers, mostly on their phones — using it at night on the couch, ordering for tomorrow
The feeling it should give: warm, homemade, simple
It must NOT feel like: a chain like Starbucks
My existing brand: none
References I like and why: none, I don't have any and I don't know what I like
